posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Santa Guise keeps showing up via random. Maybe it's because I forgot him during that big "every villain" thing. c.c Anyway, today he led Sky-Scraper, Captain Cosmic, TLT and Bunker in another advanced Citizen Dawn campaign, this time in the Dok'thorath Capital. It wasn't a good idea. :( Believe it or not, Guise made everything worse.
 
So then it was off to Atlantis, where Chono-Ranger, F6 Tempest and Omnitron-U took on Voss's advanced army. How do you say "it was a complete rout" in Atlantean?
 
But heroes never give up! How about F6 Unity, Scholar and F6 AZ fighting advanced Plague Rat in the Enclave? He got in some good hits, and the heroes were hurting, but he ended up rethinking his life choices by the end.
 
Baron Blade got advanced angry and tried to BOMB CHAOS. He was actually pretty good at it, and helped out Omnitron-U, Visionary and TLT on the first round. Tachyon crushed him a few rounds later for his hubris.
 
Then it off to the Time Cataclysm! Advanced Skinwalker versus Guise, Scholar of the Infinite, Argent Adept, Nightmist and the Wraith! Do you know, if Nightmist is in Mist Form and Oppressive Smog is out, Skinny G will slowly destroy himself on his flip side? Well, unless the Pouch of Bones is out. Nightmist can do a looot of damage to Gloomy and his army all on her lonesome, though. Sadly, it was not enough to win the day, and thus despair reigned across all of time and space, the end.
 
Lately, I've taken to setting up games to play out final battles from superhero movies, TV shows, etc. Today, it was Suicide Squad, starring Chrono-Ranger as Rick Flag, DW Expatriette as Deadshot, Guise as Harley Quinn, Haka as Killer Croc and Ra as El Diablo, fighting Gloomweaver (cuz I didn't feel like a Matriarch battle) in Megalopolis, because those movies are always in cities. It was a quick and easy relic victory. I can't remember the last time I got that much use out of Wrathful Gaze! Also, Suicide Squad was just kind of okay, for the record.

A challenge I've wanted to try for a while is beating Heroic Infinitor on his Overcome by Manifestations side, after purposefully 'incapping' him. posts.cooked:
Lordy.

AZ, Young Legacy, F6 Bunker, Eternal Haka, and Freedom Wraith dove underwater to deal with an Advanced Matriarch in the Ruins of Atlantis.

 

It started out pretty easy.  Legacy had Fortitude and Lead from the Front quickly, and spent a great deal of time tanking damage.  Huginn came out quickly, but Munnin did not, and she had opened with one of her Horrid Cacophonies before we'd played anything, so we got set up for beat downs without problem.  And then a Ground Pound - Internal Combustion boardwipe combo was interupted by a Leaking Room (Bunker was before Haka, you see), and things started going to hell.  The Leaking Room was followed by a Horrid Cacophony which wiped our defenses, and then a Phosphorescent Chamber on the next round, which dropped our health from the 20s to single digits across the board.  We almost won that round, but Haka of Battle isn't much use without a damaging power, which Eternal Haka lacked.  So I held on a Rampage and prayed Haka could survive until the next round.  And then the environment played Mystical Defenses.  Which wiped the birdies, and started dishing out damage to us.  And we didn't have Lead from the Front anymore to protect us.  Fortunately, we did have Smoke Bombs, and enough equipment hanging around to avoid the Matriarch's damage.  So everyone was brought down to 6 hp, where we stayed as everyone was simultaneously the lowest hp.  (Which, incidentally, takes a ridiculously long time to resolve.  For every bird destroyed, for each Carrion Field, I had to first pick the highest hp.  Then I had to "choose for me" the order the rest would be damaged.  Then I had to, for four heroes, agree that that hero was the lowest hp, and then pick the "highest hp" hero.  That's 10 choices per carrion field, or 20 choices per dying bird, or about 200 choices overall.)

Finally I survived the environment turn.  Matriarch's turn was mercifully boring, and I passed along to Haka, who rampaged over her face to victory.

First time playing the physical game, and it turned into a lengthy and exciting battle.

Setback, Bunker and the Sentinels took on Gloomweaver and his cult in the Realm of Discord. An early Pouch of Bones and a Vast Following the turn after we destroyed it made it hard for anything to stick (the Profane Zealots didn't help, either) and we spent most of our time just keeping the zombies and cultists at bay thanks to Time Flies -- unfortunately, also thanks to Time Flies, the other two Relics quickly made it out and Gloomweaver flipped. Fortunately by this point, everyone was pretty well set up -- all four Signatures were out, as well as Looking Up, High-Risk Behavior and Silver Lining and Bunker had been reaping obscene amounts of cards thanks to Ammo Drops the whole game.

Writhe's signature got a lot of use. It turns out if Setback is one of the heroes in a 3-H game, Writhe and Mainstay end up as highest HP PDQ (and thanks to their signatures and Dr. Medico, they can stay there a long time). It let Setback keep being High Risky (at one point he had a +4) and kept Gloomweaver punching himself via pins. Things finally broke out for us when -- after the last Vast Following was in the trash -- we killed the Pouch of Bones and we combined for about 50 damage in one round (Yay, Omni-Cannon), Silver-Lining'd Setback to highest HP (he had so many tokens that even with Gloomy's damage reduced to 0, it killed Setback), and finally put Gloomweaver down.

It took us close to two hours, but it was a great time.

posts.name: Donner
posts.cooked:
The Dark Watch team is full of redirection synergy.  Crowbar to 1 target, then to Nightmist with an amulet.  Jack Handle Setback with multiple Friendly Fires.  RPG Launcher a target and Nightmist.  Oblivion of 2 or less with Driving Mantis and Wrong Time and Place in play.  Your team takes nothing and someone gets targeted for huge damage.  Expatriette may seem like the least synergistic, but she has the easiest time feeding Setback's "Whoops!  Sorry!", although Mr. Fixer can, too, with Tool Box and Bloody Knuckles. 

Their Dark Watch promos are a bit harder to deal with.  The best here is DW Expatriette, followed by DW Fixer.  DW Setback is great with no tokens (but leaves you token starved) or with lots of tokens and no other ongoings.  Plays slower but a bit more predictable and safe.  Otherwise his other ongoings eclipse things.  DW Nightmist is great for setting up her spells for the next turn, but otherwise is better off using Tome of Magic (or whatever it's called) for the extra card each round if using either of her amulets.
